native_interfaces.semantics_assumed: The active init/update/finalize path returns the standard BLAKE3 extendable-output hash of exactly the supplied bytes; a 32-byte request returns the standard 256-bit digest. The FFI respects Lean ownership, lifetime, array-size, and C-ABI contracts. Uncalled keyed, derive-key, and version exports are covered because importing Blake3.Rust makes them reachable to downstream Lean code, but Compilatr.ix does not currently rely on their results. The sibling Blake3.C module binds the vendored C implementation behind six c_blake3_* externs; Compilatr.ix does not import it, so they are inventoried as present-but-unimported and any drift in the package tree's extern set fails the check.
native_interfaces.proof_effect: Content addresses use this result operationally. There is no Lean theorem connecting the returned bytes to a pure BLAKE3 specification, so collision resistance and conformance are explicit assumptions rather than proved facts. Generic evaluator readdressing, HPT evaluator and case-binder-field concretization, owner-sensitive case pruning, exact scalar fetch forwarding, local PAP/application refinement, and the rooted-restriction fuel induction are hash-independent and remain in the ordinary logical axiom set, while the indexed production addressed-lowering, checked HPT cache/summary/accepted-result/consumer theorem cones, and public reachability theorems that validate an exact input digest intentionally expose Blake3.HasherOps.hash._native.native_decide.ax_1✝ because they consume actual native digests; Compilatrix/Fence.lean pins that exact exception. The opaque FFI declarations also cross a proof-bearing subtype boundary for output length. Canonical IxIR2 snapshot byte-codec laws use only existing logical axioms; addressed ingress and exact checked-source program/context recovery retain this same native hash exception, with an explicit pairwise collision premise for recovering artifact equality from root equality. Modular source context transport uses exact binding equality and only ordinary logical axioms; its assembled closed-source theorem retains the same production BLAKE3 dependency. Reuse also compares full finite contexts, and serialized source records reconstruct proofs through the ordinary checker. Indexed whole-program IxIR1 addressing proves exact equality with the original semantic and exact-source audit predicates, including malformed inputs. Its prepared lookup indexes retain first-binding precedence and reverse preimages; the returned compilation certificate and native hash exception are unchanged. Modular source preparation retains a proof of successful canonical-address validation only for exact owned entries, and shares a completed preparation within certificate production and checking. Full fresh-checker equality covers current context and policy rejection behavior; canonical facts do not replace dependency, usage, literal, or resource checks. Persisted records reconstruct canonical evidence afresh. Three additional exact fences retain the existing logical and native BLAKE3 basis; source queries, certificate bytes, native symbols, and native contracts are unchanged. The backend-independent checked Ixon erasure prefix exposes the same native hash dependency; Ixby lowering admission, total data equality, reference determinism, and fixed-input value/byte execution refinement introduce no new native boundary. Reusable Ixby symbolic substitution and value/byte reflection quantify over all admitted opaque-data argument arrays using only ordinary logical axioms; runtime data inspection remains outside the checked fragment.
trust_basis: The v3 checker also uses Blake3.Rust.Hasher.init, update and finalizeWithLength for tagged node and context preimages. They resolve to the same three active native symbols; no keyed or derive-key operation is used. An explicit kernel proof discharges the 32-byte output bound, and eight exact input/literal fences retain the existing axiom basis.

specification_assumptions.assumption: The v3 schema, adapted resource rules and anonymous typechecking algorithms match argumentcomputer/ix jcb/ix-compilatrix at 0a31c8dbc63755924c645bf1afedc563e395e88a, with documented consumer bounds and raw-byte adapters. This source revision is independent of the Aiur target pin. Executing the checker does not provide a whole-checker semantic soundness theorem, backend simulation or an IxVM resource proof.
specification_assumptions.proof_effect: Twenty-five exact fences cover contract roundtrips, quantity laws and scope/owner/loan invariants; two cover the original resource-input equations. Eight more cover literal-pin soundness and combined-input equations, and four cover byte-indexed catalog load, scope, root and typing equations, retaining only ordinary logic and the existing BLAKE3 native exception. Explicit kernel proofs discharge hash-length bounds. No native interface or axiom is added; existing v2 backend proof domains are unchanged.
trust_basis: Usage, input ownership and relative locality remain independent. Arrow result contracts and borrow-let kinds are preserved in addressed bytes; no v2 ownership inference or implicit projection is applied.

Strict bounded decoding validates canonical expressions/constants, sorted environment tables, object hashes, complete constant roots, main membership and hint indices. Presentation metadata is outside anonymous admission.

The resource adapter rebuilds references and sharing from raw bytes and binds external interfaces, shareable types, choice behavior, literal pins and checker limits to a canonical profile. No cached materialization grants facts.

ValidatedInput retains successful resource, literal-profile and erased-typing equations over the same decoded byte-indexed source. Its checkClaim binds the native Resource subject/profile after these checks. ResourceInput.checkClaimBinding alone remains a binding check.

The typechecker always verifies raw materializations, checks every constant key, rejects sharing cycles and empty/orphan blocks, and applies finite consumer conversion/count/dispatch/fuel bounds. No frontend FFI, parallel worker native shim, metadata ingress or egress dependency is imported.

Catalog admission requires manifest version 2, object format 3 and validator 1 (erased-lean-v1), verifies original piece hashes/roots/sizes and aggregate budgets, resolves union assumptions and typechecks every union constant. Fat overlap deduplicates equal bytes; chunked input requires complete sorted member witnesses authenticated by committed roots/counts, first-owner assignment, disjoint chunks and full coverage. Hints min-merge, mains are unique-or-absent, and opaque metadata grants no proof. Validator 1 grants no resource profile or backend optimization.
The selected state proofs do not justify stack allocation, region allocation, RC elimination or arbitrary backend ownership conversion. These require their own source-bound refinement.

specification_assumptions.scope: Compilatrix.X86 typed AST, independent byte decoder, and executable local semantics
specification_assumptions.assumption: For sequential x86-64 v0 executions that satisfy the compiler ABI invariants and use canonical mapped user addresses, the local register, permissioned little-endian memory, stack, comparison/branch, flag producer/consumer, and architectural-fault behavior (memory faults and div's #DE) agrees with corresponding 64-bit user-mode behavior at Compilatr.ix observations. Misaligned-call, stack-mismatch, corrupt-return, and callee-saved-clobber outcomes are compiler-contract failures that must be proved unreachable, not hardware exceptions. E2 relates symbolic PCs and return tokens to byte RIP and physical stack slots under explicit access conditions and accounts for the final physical RET. Agreement of the local byte model with a reference ISA, including unified instruction fetch and canonical-address faults, remains unproved.
specification_assumptions.proof_effect: Lean theorems about the local semantics use only ordinary logical axioms and do not assert hardware correctness. Any native-correctness claim that treats the local model as its reference is conditional on this specification assumption until the emitted-fragment bridge is proved.
trust_basis: Intel 64 and IA-32 Software Developer's Manual combined instruction-set reference, version 092
AMD64 Architecture Programmer's Manual Volume 3, revision 3.37

Op.rows lists every row the table may emit or decode; the typed constructors choose listed rows (Instr.*_wellFormed) and exclude signed division, floating point, SIMD, atomics, indirect calls, raw syscalls, TLS, high-byte registers, rsp SIB indices, and byte-width imul

Certified production emission does not use that assumption: acceptance proves every decoded operation, boundary, canonical block offset, signed internal target, and exact runtime relocation inventory. Internal-call execution uses the explicit SafeTrace stack/data-access conditions. Runtime CALL transfer is proved after checked PC32 application; execution of external procedure bodies requires their separate semantic/ABI contracts.

ObjectEval lifts these results through serialized ELF, and the N2 Output.sourceRefinesObjects endpoint consumes them for every admitted runtime Word list. No new Lean axiom or native FFI symbol is introduced. Encoder completeness and unchecked raw API results are not claimed.
